Two Big Debuts Fail To Boost Stocks
 
Plus, cyber fears hit financials and Williams-Sonoma gets cooked
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
MICHAEL M. SANTIAGO/GETTY IMAGES
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

A successful Anthropic initial public offering failed to ignite a rally. The Nasdaq Composite was down 2.3% on Thursday, and the S&P 500 was off by 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 1101 points, or 2.2%. The S&P 500 sold off across sectors, led by a 3% decline in consumer-discretionary stocks.

 

Anthropic’s shares soared in their debut. After pricing at $83 on Wednesday evening, shares of the maker of Claude jumped 17% in first-day trading. At session’s end, Anthropic’s valuation, on a fully-diluted basis, was around $1.8 trillion.

 

Grand Theft Auto’s maker stumbled on the game’s launch day. The hugely anticipated arrival of ‘GTA VI’ failed to boost the shares of the company releasing the videogame. Take-Two Interactive Software was down 3.7% on Thursday, and is off by more than 18% on the year.

 

A cyberattack spooked financial stocks. Data from some customers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase were leaked by a ransomware group, but the information was limited and services were not disrupted. Shares of Visa fell 3%, and S&P 500 financials overall were down 1.5%. There was another rally in cybersecurity stocks. Palo Alto Networks rose 6.4%, which led the S&P 500.

 

Williams-Sonoma led decliners in the S&P 500. The retailer is another victim of weak home sales. It reported a slowdown in revenue growth at its flagship brand, Pottery Barn. Shares fell over 15%.

 

Gold and silver hit their lowest prices in over a year. Expectations of rising interest rates have hit the precious metals, which makes them less attractive. Gold ended the day lower, at $3,682 per troy ounce. The ten-year Treasury yield held above 5%, ending the session at 5.051%.

One Big Story

 
 
CARLOS BARRIA/REUTERS
 

What will Anthropic market value be following its initial public offering? This might seem like a newbie investor question. But in the case of a giant IPO like Anthropic, it is anything but simple.

 

As investors start to trade the AI company’s shares on Thursday, they may encounter some very different market-capitalization figures, depending on what source they are using. And the numbers can differ not by a hair or two, but by hundreds of billions of dollars. At the opening trading price, that ranges from just under $1.5 trillion to just over $2 trillion.

 

Such gaps between valuation measures for an IPO aren’t unusual. But for Anthropic, they can be complex because of some unique ways the company has been structured and funded.
